definition: A Large-scale ImaGe and Noisy-Text Embedding, 1.8 Billion Image-Text pairs dataset by Google.
details: A Large-scale ImaGe and Noisy-Text Embedding, 1.8 Billion Image-Text pairs dataset by Google.

explainer.lead: ALIGN is a Google image-and-text embedding approach built around 1.8 billion image–text pairs. It places pictures and written descriptions in a shared numerical space, helping computers connect visual content with language at very large scale.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a huge box of photos, each with a short note that may be messy or imperfect. ALIGN learns a way to give matching photos and notes similar codes, so a computer can connect what it sees with words. Its training collection contains 1.8 billion photo-and-note pairs.
tiers.practitioner: ALIGN is applied by encoding images and text into a common embedding space for vision–language tasks such as matching and retrieval. Its scale is central to the approach, but the text is noisy, so a close match should not automatically be treated as a clean or factual annotation.
tiers.paperLevel: Let D = {(I_i, T_i)} for i = 1, …, 1.8B denote the image–text collection. ALIGN learns image and text representations whose outputs can be compared in a shared embedding space. The scale supports broad representation learning, while noisy text introduces imperfect supervision and can limit the reliability of individual pairings.

explainer.example: Given an image of a dog running on a beach and the noisy caption “dog beach run,” ALIGN represents both in the same space. Their representations can then be compared with those of unrelated image–text pairs.

usedIn.name: Image–text retrieval
usedIn.detail: Shared embeddings support finding text related to an image or images related to text.

usedIn.name: Vision–language research
usedIn.detail: ALIGN provides a large-scale approach to connecting visual and textual representations.

usedIn.name: Representation learning
usedIn.detail: Its 1.8 billion noisy image–text pairs illustrate learning from web-scale, imperfect supervision.

flow: Collect paired images and noisy text.
Compare both in a shared space.
explainer.origin: ALIGN is by Google, and its name expands to “A Large-scale ImaGe and Noisy-Text Embedding.” Its defining collection contains 1.8 billion image–text pairs.
explainer.whyItMatters: ALIGN shows how image–text understanding can be learned at enormous scale without requiring every text description to be clean. A shared embedding space gives pictures and language a common basis for comparison.
